questionText:
Read the following case study and answer the question:

"A corporate compliance firm conducted a training seminar reviewing Stanley Milgram's classic 1963 Yale University obedience experiments. Participants were reminded that ordinary citizens, assigned the role of 'Teacher', delivered what they believed were escalating, painful electric shocks (from 15 to 450 volts) to an innocent 'Learner' strapped to a chair whenever errors were made. Despite hearing the learner scream in agony and eventually fall silent, 65% of participants delivered the maximum 450-volt lethal shock under the firm prods of an authority figure in a grey lab coat ('The experiment requires that you continue'). The seminar examined subsequent experimental variations: when the authority gave orders via telephone, obedience plummeted to 20%; when the teacher was forced to physically hold the learner's hand onto a shock plate, obedience dropped to 30%; and when two rebellious confederate teachers refused to obey, compliance collapsed to 10%."

questionText:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(A) Status
(B) Norms
(C) Roles
(D) Cohesiveness

List-II
(I) Expected standards of behavior and beliefs
(II) Mutual attraction among group members
(III) Relative social position given to group members by others
(IV) Socially defined expectations

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
1. Status: The relative social position, prestige, or ranking accorded to group members by others (III); 2. Norms: Shared, expected standards of behavior and beliefs that guide member conduct (I); 3. Roles: Socially defined expectations and behavioral prescriptions associated with a specific position in the group (IV); 4. Cohesiveness: The interpersonal forces and mutual attraction binding members together into a unified team (II). This gives (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II).
Hence, option (C) is the correct match.
